The method / Look legitimate online / Step 1
ACTION 17 OF 32 · PHASE 05

Choose a name customers can understand and remember

Help buyers connect the name to the service, without becoming generic or unprotectable.

WHEN TO DO THISAfter the value proposition is clear, before buying the domain.ESTIMATED WORK TIME30–60 min
↗
Your one job

Help buyers connect the name to the service, without becoming generic or unprotectable.

01

Do this now

  1. 01

    Write the service category, primary customer, location, brand tone and likely search phrases.

  2. 02

    Generate short, pronounceable names and test them verbally with actual people.

  3. 03

    Check search results, existing local business records, domain/social availability and potential trademark conflicts.

  4. 04

    Choose a primary name and, separately, a truthful descriptive tagline. A domain can emphasize search intent without renaming the legal business.

02

Copy this into ChatGPT

Replace anything in [square brackets] with your real business details. The prompt is a shortcut, not a substitute for the steps above.

READY-TO-USE PROMPT
Act as a naming strategist for [BUSINESS OFFER] serving [CUSTOMER] in [COUNTRY]. Generate 15 short brand names in three categories: clear descriptive, distinctive premium, and locally relevant. For each explain pronunciation, memorable customer benefit, likely search terms and risks. Then give me a research checklist for current domain, handle, registry and trademark availability. Do not claim any name is available without checking.
03

Finish with this

A shortlisted, screened name plus tagline and domain options.

Before moving on, check your work against the following:

  • Name is understandable and easy to say
  • Search/domain/trademark checks are tracked
  • Tagline describes the real offer
DON’T MAKE THIS MISTAKE

Choosing a name solely because an AI model says it will rank #1.

READY TO MOVE ON?

A real customer can find, understand and contact the business consistently from mobile.
